question: A differential equation representing the family of parabolas with axis parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo></math>axis and whose length of latus rectum is the distance of the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> from the line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, is given by:
solution:
The equation of family of parabolas

(x-α)2=4a(y-β)
Distance of point (2,-3) from line 3x+4y=5 is
4a=3×2+4×-3−55

4a=6−12−55

4a=115

(x−α)2=115(y−β)
Differentiate w.r.t. x
2(x−α)=115dydx

Again diff. w. r. t. x

2=115d2ydx2

11d2ydx2=10
